hints.title: Bitmask Character Set Representation
hints.text: Since only lowercase English letters appear, a 26-bit integer can uniquely encode the set of characters present in any word.

hints.title: Bitwise AND Disjointness Check
hints.text: Two words share no letters if and only if the bitwise and of their respective bitmasks is zero.

hints.title: Mask Reduction and Pair Product Scan
hints.text: Map each mask to its maximum word length. Compare all pairs of unique masks; if maskA and maskB is zero, update maximum product.

hints.title: See the blueprint

variables: U: unique mask count (<= 2^26, typically small)
complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(L + U^2) time and O(U) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Pairwise string comparisons require O(N^2 * L) operations, which times out for large word lists.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Precomputing bitmasks compresses 26 character set checks into a single constant-time bitwise AND operation.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should deduplicate masks by keeping the maximum length per identical character set.
